name: The Sun (Sol)
summary: The gravitational center of our planetary system, fusing 600 million tons of hydrogen into helium every second in its core.

name: Mercury
summary: The smallest and innermost planet, characterized by a cratered silicate crust and an unusually large metallic iron core.

name: Venus
summary: Earth's sister world under a runaway greenhouse effect, blanketed by opaque sulfuric acid clouds and extreme atmospheric pressures.

name: Earth & Moon
summary: Only known celestial body hosting surface liquid water and an active nitrogen-oxygen biosphere, stabilized by its large lunar companion.

name: Mars
summary: A cold, iron oxide-rich desert world possessing the solar system's largest volcano (Olympus Mons) and evidence of ancient lacustrine environments.

name: Jupiter
summary: The dominant planetary mass of the solar system, featuring alternating ammonia cloud bands, persistent anticyclones, and 95 known moons.

name: Saturn
summary: Distinguished by an expansive, highly reflective ring system of water ice particles and shepherd moons spanning up to 282,000 km.

name: Uranus
summary: An ice giant world with a dynamic methane atmosphere and an extreme 97.8° axial tilt that causes retrograde, on-its-side rotation.

name: Neptune
summary: The outermost major planet, driven by supersonic atmospheric zonal winds reaching up to 2,100 km/h and high-altitude methane cirrus clouds.

name: Oort Cloud Reservoir
summary: A vast spherical swarm of volatile-rich icy planetesimals marking the outer gravitational frontier of Sol.

scientific_details.composition: Water ice, methane, ammonia, carbon monoxide

name: Alpha Centauri System
summary: Our nearest stellar neighbors, consisting of binary pair Rigil Kentaurus (G2V) and Toliman (K1V), orbited distantly by Proxima Centauri.

scientific_details.exoplanets: Proxima b, Proxima c, Proxima d

name: Sirius (The Dog Star)
summary: The brightest apparent star in Earth's night sky, paired with 'the Pup', a dense degenerate carbon-oxygen white dwarf.

name: Vega (Alpha Lyrae)
summary: A luminous, rapid rotator bulging significantly at its equator, surrounded by a warm circumstellar dust debris ring.

name: Betelgeuse (Alpha Orionis)
summary: A pulsating red supergiant near the end of its stellar evolution, destined to undergo core-collapse into a Type II supernova.

name: Pleiades (Seven Sisters)
summary: An open cluster of mid-B type hot blue stars moving through an interstellar dust cloud, illuminating a faint reflection nebulosity.

name: Sagittarius A*
summary: The 4-million-solar-mass gravitational anchor at the nucleus of the Milky Way, shadowed by an intensely sheared synchrotron accretion flow.

name: Andromeda Galaxy (M31)
summary: The largest galaxy in our Local Group, containing roughly one trillion stars and currently approaching the Milky Way at 110 km/s.

name: Virgo Supercluster Hub
summary: A massive gravitational gathering of thousands of galaxies, within which the Local Group occupies a small outer filament.

name: SMACS J0723.3-7327
summary: A colossal foreground galaxy cluster that acts as a natural cosmic telescope, bending and magnifying light from galaxies over 13 billion light years away.

scientific_details.lens_phenomenon: Relativistic Einstein rings and tangential arcs

name: Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB)
summary: The surface of last scattering: relic thermal radiation emitted 380,000 years after the Big Bang, marking the absolute visual edge of the observable universe.
